# Generating Functions

## 1. MGFS in R

Recall

$$
M_{x} (t) = \mathbb{E}(e^{tX})
$$

For discrete random variable

$$
M_{x}(t) = \sum_{x} e^{tX} P(X=x)
$$

For a continous random variable

$$
M_{x}(t) = \int e^{tX}P(X=x)
$$

### Binomial Distribution

$$
X \sim Bin(n,p)
$$

The theoretical MGF is

$$
M_{x}(t) = (1-p+pe^{t})^{n}
$$

```{r}
mgf_binomial <- function(t, n, p) {
  (1 - p + p * exp(t))^n
}

mgf_binomial(0.5, n = 10, p = 0.3)
```

Numerical Verification

```{r}
mgf_empirical <- function(t, x, prob) {
  sum(exp(t * x) * prob)
}

x <- 0:10
prob <- dbinom(x, size = 10, prob = 0.3)

mgf_empirical(0.5, x, prob)
```

## Mgf of Poisson Distribution

$$
X \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda) 
$$

$$
M_{x} (t) = e^{\lambda(t - \lambda)} \qquad t \in[1, \infty]
$$

```{r}
mgf_poisson <- function(t,lambda){
  return(exp(lambda*(t - 1)))
}

mgf_poisson(0.2,lambda = 5)
```

Using MGFs to Obtain Moments

```{r}
library(numDeriv)

M <- function(t) mgf_poisson(t,5)
Mean_est <- grad(M,0)
second_moment <- hessian(M,0)

Mean_est
second_moment
```

Implementing PGFs: We need to know the PGFs before using `numDeriv` as it helps us to compute the moments

$$
X \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda)
$$

$$
G(s) = e^{\lambda(s-1}
$$

```{r}
lambda <- 4
G <- function (s) {
  exp(lambda*(s-1))
}
# mean
means <- grad(G,1)
means
# Second Der
second_der <- hessian(G,1)
second_der
# variance
vars <- (second_der) + (means) - (means)^2
vars
```
